errors.fallback: The request could not be completed.

status.network: The SSO did not respond. Check your connection and try again.
status.unauthorized: Your session ended. Sign in again to continue.
status.forbidden: Your role does not allow this action.
status.notFound: The record was not found. It may have been removed.
status.conflict: A record with these values already exists.

status.tooManyRequests: Too many requests in a short time. Wait a moment and try again.

code.client_key_not_found: The key was not found or is already revoked.
code.client_key_required: Register at least one client key before activating the project.
code.client_keys_empty: This project has no client keys yet.
code.csrf_token_invalid: Your security token is out of date. Reload the page and try again.
code.duplicate: A record with these values already exists.
code.internal_error: The SSO could not process the request. Nothing was changed.
code.member_not_found: This person is no longer a member of the project.
code.origin_not_allowed: This request did not come from the console and was refused.
code.project_has_members: Add no one else and remove the members of this project before deleting it.
code.project_has_routes: Delete the routes of this project before deleting it.
code.project_not_found: This project does not exist. It may have been removed.
code.public_key_invalid: This is not a valid public key.
code.public_key_too_short: The RSA key must have at least 2048 bits.
code.redirect_uri_not_found: This redirect URI does not exist. It may have been removed.
code.role_not_found: This role does not exist. It may have been removed.
code.role_not_in_project: This role belongs to another project.
code.role_route_project_mismatch: The role and the route belong to different projects.
code.route_not_found: This route does not exist. It may have been removed.
code.sso_access_denied: Your account has no role in the SSO project.
code.sso_last_superadmin: The SSO project needs at least one SUPERADMIN. Give the role to someone else first.
code.sso_project_protected: The SSO project runs the administration of every application. Only its SUPERADMIN changes its routes, roles, permissions, members, redirect URIs and keys, and some changes are refused to everyone.
code.sso_redirect_uri_in_use: This console signs in through this address. Delete it from a console running at another address.
code.sso_redirect_uri_last: The SSO project needs at least one redirect URI. Add the new address before deleting this one.
code.user_has_projects: This user still has access to a project. Remove the memberships first.
code.user_not_found: This user does not exist. It may have been removed.
code.validation_failed: The SSO refused some of the values sent. Check the form and try again.
code.invalid_credentials: Email or password does not match.
code.account_locked: Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
code.password_refused: The new password was refused. Use at least 12 varied characters.
code.password_not_issued: This account has no password issued.
code.login_step_expired: This step expired. Start the sign-in again.
code.no_pending_request: There is no pending sign-in request in this browser.

field.public_key_not_pem: Paste a public key in PEM format, starting with -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----.
field.role_name_invalid: Use 2 to 40 characters: an uppercase letter, then uppercase letters, digits or underscores.

forms.roleNamePattern: Use 2 to 40 capital letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter.
forms.roleNameTaken: This project already has a role with this name.

no_pending_request.title: There is no sign-in waiting here
no_pending_request.description: Open the application you want to use. It will bring you back to this page.

request_expired.title: The sign-in request expired
request_expired.description: A request lasts five minutes. Go back to the application and start again.

account_not_registered.title: This Google account is not registered
account_not_registered.description: Ask an administrator to add your e-mail to the SSO, then try again.

email_not_verified.title: Your Google e-mail is not verified
email_not_verified.description: Verify the address in your Google account and try again.

account_mismatch.title: This is not the Google account linked to you
account_mismatch.description: Use the Google account from your first sign-in, or ask an administrator to unlink it.

provider_denied.title: Sign-in was cancelled
provider_denied.description: Google did not share your identity. Choose the provider again when you are ready.

provider_error.title: Google could not complete the sign-in
provider_error.description: Nothing was changed. Try again in a moment.

generic.title: Sign-in could not be completed
generic.description: Go back to the application and try again.

unavailable.title: The SSO is not responding
unavailable.description: Nothing was changed. Reload this page in a moment.

change.title: Set your password
change.description: The password you received works once. From here on, only you know it.
change.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.

enroll.title: Set up the second factor
enroll.description: Scan the code with your authenticator app and type the six digits it shows.

mfa.title: Two step verification
mfa.description: Type the code from your authenticator app.
mfa.hint: No app at hand? Use a recovery code.

recovery.title: Keep your recovery codes
recovery.description: Each one works once, and they are the only way back if you lose the app. They show up only now.

callback.failedTitle: This sign-in could not be completed
callback.failedDescription: The link that brought you here is no longer valid. Start again and you will return to the console.

noAccess.title: You don't have access to the SSO console
noAccess.descriptionAs: You are signed in as {name} ({email}), but this account has no role in the SSO project. Ask an administrator for access.
noAccess.description: Your account has no role in the SSO project. Ask an administrator for access.

unavailable.title: The SSO is not responding
unavailable.description: The console could not reach the SSO. Nothing was changed. Try again in a moment.
unavailable.stillTitle: The SSO is still not responding
unavailable.stillDescription: Check that the service is running, then try again.

forbidden.title: You cannot open this page
forbidden.description: Your role does not include this area. Ask an administrator if you need it.

notFound.title: This page does not exist
notFound.description: The address may be mistyped, or the page moved. The menu on the side has everything your role can open.

dashboard.description: The state of the SSO catalogue, from what your role can read.
dashboard.nothingDescription: Your role opens the console, but does not read any part of the catalogue.
dashboard.loadFailed: Part of the overview could not be loaded

pending.title: Waiting for activation
pending.description: Registered in the catalogue, but unable to use the SSO until an administrator activates them.
pending.emptyDescription: Every registered project is active, or was suspended on purpose.

projects.description: Applications connected to the SSO. A project starts pending and only uses the SSO after an administrator activates it.
projects.emptyDescription: Register the first application that will sign people in through the SSO.
projects.createDescription: It starts pending. After creating, add a redirect URI and a client key, then activate it.
projects.renameDescription: The name appears on the sign-in screen, as the application people are signing in to.
projects.deleteMessage: The project leaves the catalogue with its identity. The SSO refuses while it still has routes or members.
projects.createdDescription: Next: a redirect URI and a client key, then activation.

filters.title: Filters
filters.none: {count} project, no filter | {count} projects, no filter

project.loadFailed: The project could not be loaded
project.activateMessage: Applications with this client ID can start signing people in right away.
project.suspendMessage: Every application with this client ID stops signing people in, and refresh tokens stop renewing. The catalogue stays as it is.

identity.title: Identity
identity.description: How applications and people identify this project.
identity.clientIdHint: Public identifier. Applications send it as client_id; the proof is their private key.
identity.selfNote: This is the SSO's own project: it signs in the administrators of every application. It cannot be renamed, suspended or deleted, and only its SUPERADMIN changes its routes, roles, permissions, members, redirect URIs and keys.

checklist.title: Ready to use the SSO
checklist.active: This project is active. Applications with its client ID can sign people in.
checklist.ready: Everything required is in place. Activating lets the application start signing people in.
checklist.notReady: A project only uses the SSO after activation, and activation needs the required items below.

redirect.label: Redirect URI registered
redirect.empty: The SSO only returns a sign-in to a registered address.

key.label: Active client key
key.empty: The application proves who it is by signing with the private half.

routes.label: Routes registered
routes.empty: A route that is not in the catalogue answers 404 to everyone, as if it did not exist.

grants.label: Routes granted to a role
grants.done: {count} role with permissions | {count} roles with permissions
grants.empty: Permissions connect a role to the routes it unlocks.

members.label: People with access
members.empty: Only members can sign in to this application.

redirectUris.title: Redirect URIs
redirectUris.description: The SSO only returns a sign-in to these addresses, compared character by character. Register each environment separately.
redirectUris.emptyDescription: Without one, no application can complete a sign-in with this project.
redirectUris.selfNote: This console signs in through these addresses, so they are never edited: add the new address, then delete the old one. The last address, and the one this console is using now, cannot be deleted. Only a SUPERADMIN of the SSO adds or deletes them.
redirectUris.dialogDescription: Scheme, host, port and path, exactly as the application sends it. A trailing slash makes it a different address.
redirectUris.useHttp: Use a full http or https address.
redirectUris.deleteOnly: {uri} is the only address of {project}. Until another one is added, nobody can sign in to it.
redirectUris.deleteMessage: Applications that still send {uri} stop signing in, and codes already issued to it are refused.

routes.title: Routes
routes.description: What this application exposes, grouped by path. Pick any path to see its methods and who can call it.
routes.emptyDescription: Register the routes of the application, then grant them to roles.
routes.selfNote: These are the SSO's own routes. Only a SUPERADMIN of the SSO changes them.
routes.notFoundDescription: {path} is not in the {project} catalogue. It may have been renamed or deleted.
routes.selectDescription: Pick any path in the tree to see its methods, the roles that reach it and who can call it.
routes.dialogDescription: The path as the application declares it, without the global prefix. Use :name for parameters.
routes.pathError: Start with a slash and leave no spaces, like /equipment/:id.
routes.deleteMessage: {method} {path} leaves the catalogue. The application then answers 404 to everyone on it, as if it did not exist.

routeDetail.groupLead: Not a registered route. It gathers the {count} path below that starts with this prefix, and answers no request by itself. | Not a registered route. It gathers the {count} paths below that start with this prefix, and answers no request by itself.

access.title: Access
access.description: Which role may call each method of this path. A method no role reaches answers 404 to everyone, as if it did not exist, and a granted method cannot be deleted until its grants are removed.
access.emptyDescription: Create a role in Roles & permissions, then grant this path to it here.

callers.title: Who can call it
callers.description: Members whose role reaches at least one method of this path, and which methods.
callers.emptyGranted: The roles that reach this path have no members yet.
callers.emptyNotGranted: Grant a role above. Until then, every method answers 404.

below.title: Below this path
below.description: Paths that start with this one. Pick any to open it.

grants.grantFailed: The route could not be granted
grants.revokeFailed: The permission could not be removed
grants.bulkFailed: Not every {method} route could be granted

roles.title: Roles & permissions
roles.description: Each role unlocks the routes checked below, grouped by path. Changes apply on the next request, without anyone signing in again.
roles.emptyDescription: Create the roles this application uses, then check the routes each one unlocks.
roles.rootLead: The SSO's SUPERADMIN is the root: it reaches every administrative route without any being checked, and it cannot be renamed or deleted.
roles.noRoutes: Register routes first. A role only unlocks routes that exist in the catalogue.
roles.allGetGranted: Every GET route is granted to {role}.
roles.getMissing: {count} GET route not granted to {role} yet. | {count} GET routes not granted to {role} yet.
roles.getGranted: {count} GET route granted | {count} GET routes granted
roles.deleteBlocked: Uncheck every route and move the members to another role before deleting it.
roles.selfNote: These are the SSO's own roles and permissions. Only a SUPERADMIN of the SSO changes them.
roles.addDescription: Every project starts with SUPERADMIN, ADMIN, MANAGER and VIEWER. Add the roles {project} needs; a new role starts with no routes.
roles.displayedAs: Shown as “{label}”, with the custom role icon.
roles.renameDescription: Members and permissions stay with the role. Applications only know the new name once access tokens renew, so members may be refused for up to 15 minutes.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this application, and with which role. Each person has one role per project.
members.emptyDescription: Nobody can sign in to this application yet.
members.emptyNoRoles: Create a role first. Every member joins with one.
members.addDescription: The person signs in to {project} with the role chosen here.
members.personHint: Only registered people who are not members yet.
members.lockedNote: Members of the SSO project administer every application. Only a SUPERADMIN of the SSO changes them.
members.lastRootNote: The SSO always keeps at least one SUPERADMIN: the last one cannot change role or leave.
members.peopleLoadFailed: The list of people could not be loaded
members.changeNoteSelf: The new role replaces the current one and applies to the console on the next request.
members.changeNote: The new role replaces the current one. Applications apply it when the access token renews, within 15 minutes.
members.removeSelf: You lose access to this console right away.
members.removeFromSso: {name} loses access to the SSO console on the next request.
members.removeMessage: {name} stops signing in to {project}. Their refresh tokens for it are revoked now, and an access token already issued runs out within 15 minutes.

users.description: People who can sign in through the SSO. Nobody signs in without being registered here first.
users.searchHint: Part of a name, or a complete e-mail address.
users.emptyDescription: Register the first person who will sign in through the SSO.
users.registerDescription: Registering does not grant access yet. Add the person to a project afterwards.
users.deleteMessage: {name} can no longer sign in, and any open sessions with the SSO end now. Registering the same e-mail again creates a new user.
users.registeredDescription: They can sign in once added to a project.

user.loadFailed: The user could not be loaded
user.linkedHint: Linked on the first sign-in. Another Google account with this e-mail is refused.
user.waitingHint: The first Google sign-in with this e-mail links the account.
user.addDescription: {name} signs in to the chosen project with the chosen role.
user.noRoles: This project has no roles yet.
user.rolesLoadFailed: The roles of this project could not be loaded
user.unlinkMessage: The next Google sign-in with this e-mail links a new account. Use it when the person changed Google accounts.
user.unlinkedDescription: The next Google sign-in with this e-mail links a new account.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: How this person is identified when signing in.

projects.description: Where this person can sign in, and with which role.
projects.emptyDescription: Without a project, this person cannot sign in anywhere.

credential.title: Credentials
credential.description: The password is issued here and handed to the person; the second factor they enroll on first sign-in.
credential.issuedDescription: It shows up only now. Hand it over through a safe channel: they will change it on first sign-in.
credential.pendingHint: Still the issued password; it will be changed on first sign-in.
credential.mfaPendingHint: The person enrolls it on the next sign-in.
credential.recoveryLeft: No recovery code left | {count} recovery code left | {count} recovery codes left
credential.failed: It was not possible to finish.

clientKeys.title: Client keys
clientKeys.pageDescription: Keys that applications sign with to prove who they are to the SSO. Every key belongs to one project.
clientKeys.noProjectDescription: Choose a project above to see and manage its keys.
clientKeys.description: Public halves the SSO uses to verify the application's signed assertions. The private half never comes back to the SSO.
clientKeys.emptyDescription: The application cannot authenticate to the SSO without an active key.
clientKeys.registerDescription: Generated on the application owner's machine. Only the public half is sent; the private half stays with them.
clientKeys.publicKeyHint: RSA, at least 2048 bits, in PEM (SPKI) format.
clientKeys.pemError: Paste the whole key, from -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY----- to -----END PUBLIC KEY-----.
clientKeys.expiresHint: Optional. Leave empty for a key without expiry.
clientKeys.generateMessage: The SSO creates the pair, keeps only the public half and shows you the private key once. Hand it to the owner of {project} through a secure channel.
clientKeys.secretDescription: Private key for {project}. The application loads it from its own environment, as APP_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64.
clientKeys.secretWarning: This key is shown once and is not stored in the SSO. If it passes through chat, a ticket, a commit or a CI log, revoke it and generate another.
clientKeys.secretAcknowledge: I stored this key in a safe place
clientKeys.revokeMessage: Applications signing with this key stop authenticating immediately. A revoked key cannot be restored.
